steps.intent: Egypt aims to reaffirm Jerusalem’s final-status character, preserve the historic status quo of the Holy Sites, de-escalate violence, and revive negotiations without directly confronting the United States. The difficult points will be balancing Arab demands for explicit rejection of unilateral recognition and settlement activity against US and Israeli red lines; some Council members may seek stronger language condemning the US decision or invoking Resolution 478.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supports a united Council message calling for de-escalation, but the text cannot remain silent on the illegal unilateral decision on Jerusalem. We need an explicit reaffirmation that changes to Jerusalem have no legal effect and a call on all States not to move diplomatic missions there, in line with resolution 478. We also need the Council to recall Israel's obligations to halt settlements and respect international humanitarian law.
messages.China: China supports the draft's call for de-escalation and its reaffirmation of the two-State solution. We ask the penholder to recall resolutions 476 and 478 and to state clearly that unilateral decisions altering Jerusalem's status have no legal effect and must be rescinded. We also seek an operative call for an end to Israeli settlement activities, consistent with resolution 2334, so that the Council's position remains clear and consistent with its prior decisions.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the draft’s call for de-escalation and its reaffirmation of the two-State solution, but the text must reflect the Council’s established position on Jerusalem. We ask the penholder to recall resolution 478 (1980), state clearly that decisions altering Jerusalem’s character, status or demographic composition are null and void and must be rescinded, and call on States not to establish diplomatic missions in Jerusalem. These additions are essential to preserve the status quo and the credibility of the Council.
messages.France: France supports the draft’s balanced reaffirmation of the two-State solution and its call for de-escalation. However, the Council must draw the legal consequences of the 6 December decision: we need explicit language that unilateral changes to Jerusalem’s character and status have no legal effect and that all States must not recognize them. We also ask that OP3 be aligned with resolution 2334 by referring to the 4 June 1967 lines, including with regard to Jerusalem.
messages.Italy: Italy supports the Egyptian draft as a constructive basis and welcomes its balanced call for de-escalation and respect for the status quo at the Holy Sites. We ask the penholder to add generic language on recent decisions concerning Jerusalem and to anchor the text explicitly in resolution 2334 (2016), including its paragraph 3, so that all States are called on not to prejudge final status issues. Italy can accept language that does not single out any Member State, but the Council should be clear that unilateral changes to Jerusalem's status have no legal effect.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the draft's focus on de-escalation, the two-State solution and Jerusalem as a final status issue. To give effect to resolution 2334 (2016) and the Council's established position, we ask that the text state clearly that decisions purporting to alter the character, status or demographic composition of Jerusalem have no legal effect and must be rescinded. We also support adding the call on all States to refrain from establishing diplomatic missions in Jerusalem and to comply with Council resolutions on the Holy City.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports the balanced thrust of the Egyptian draft and its emphasis on de-escalation, the two-State solution and the status quo of the Holy Sites. To reflect the Council’s existing obligations and the concerns of the broader membership, we ask the penholder to add explicit language that unilateral decisions altering Jerusalem’s character or status have no legal effect and must be rescinded, and to call on all States to comply with resolution 2334 (2016) and resolution 478 (1980). We are flexible on placement but consider these points important for our support.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the draft's balanced call for de-escalation and reaffirmation of the two-State solution. However, it is insufficient merely to recall that Jerusalem is a final-status issue; the Council should state clearly that decisions altering the city's status have no legal effect and call on all States not to move diplomatic missions to Jerusalem. We also ask that OP7 refer to direct negotiations on the Madrid/Quartet/Arab Peace Initiative basis. With these changes we can support the text.
messages.Senegal: Senegal welcomes the Egyptian draft and supports its de-escalation objectives. As a co-sponsor of resolution 2334 (2016), we ask that the text anchor itself explicitly in 2334, including the illegality of settlements and the demand that they cease. We also need a clear reaffirmation that unilateral decisions on Jerusalem have no legal effect and that all States must refrain from recognizing changes to the 1967 lines, including East Jerusalem. With these amendments Senegal can support the text.
messages.Sweden: Sweden supports the draft's de-escalation focus and can support it with amendments that restate existing Council law on Jerusalem. We ask in particular for language reaffirming that unilateral decisions altering the character, status or demographic composition of Jerusalem have no legal effect and must be rescinded, and for a call on all States to refrain from establishing diplomatic missions in Jerusalem under resolution 478. We would also want an operative call on Israel to cease settlement activity, consistent with resolution 2334, and clearer reference to Israel's obligations as the occupying Power under the Fourth Geneva Convention.
messages.Ukraine: Ukraine supports the draft as a basis and shares its balanced call for de-escalation and respect for the historic status quo. To reflect resolution 2334 (2016) and established Council practice, we ask that the text expressly reaffirm that unilateral decisions altering Jerusalem’s character or status have no legal effect and call on all States to refrain from establishing diplomatic missions in Jerusalem under resolution 478 (1980). We can support the text with this strengthening.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK supports the direction of this draft and believes it can form the basis for a balanced Council response. We would like the text to state clearly that unilateral decisions on Jerusalem have no legal effect and cannot prejudge final status, and to call on all States not to establish diplomatic missions in Jerusalem. We would also welcome a clearer reference to Israel's legitimate security concerns and the need to combat incitement, so the resolution remains balanced. We are ready to work with Egypt and other members to finalize a text that can secure the widest possible support.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the draft's balanced call for de-escalation and a two-State solution, but we cannot accept language in OP4 that could be read as implying that our recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital prejudges final status. We request the deletion or replacement of that clause and the addition of 'with agreed swaps' to OP3 to reflect the established U.S. position. We can support the text with these changes.
messages.Uruguay: Uruguay supports the draft's balanced call for de-escalation and its reaffirmation of the two-State solution, but the Council must be explicit that unilateral actions altering Jerusalem's character or status have no legal effect and cannot prejudge final status talks. We therefore ask the penholder to incorporate the relevant language from resolution 2334 (2016) and to call on all States to refrain from establishing diplomatic missions in Jerusalem. With those improvements, Uruguay is ready to support the text.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supports the current draft, which contains the essential elements we have pressed for: the null-and-void language on any alteration of Jerusalem’s character and status, the call on all States to refrain from diplomatic missions in Jerusalem, and the demand that Israel cease settlement activities. While we would have preferred an explicit reference to the United States decision of 6 December 2017, we will not insist on that point in the interest of Council unity and a strong, unified message on Jerusalem and the two-State solution.
messages.China: China supports the current text. Our key concerns on Jerusalem, resolution 478 (1980), and settlement cessation have been reflected, and the draft preserves the Council's established positions under resolution 2334 (2016). We see no need for further changes and urge the Council to act with unity and send a clear message on the need to respect the status of Jerusalem and revive credible negotiations.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the current text, which reflects our red lines on Jerusalem, including resolution 478 (1980), the null-and-void language, and the call on States to refrain from establishing diplomatic missions in Jerusalem. We welcome the balance between de-escalation, condemnation of violence and terror, and the reaffirmation of the two-State solution based on the 4 June 1967 lines. Ethiopia is ready to vote in favour if the draft is put to the Council.
messages.France: France supports the current text as it stands. The draft reflects our key priorities: immediate de-escalation, reaffirmation of resolution 2334 (2016), preservation of the 4 June 1967 lines including Jerusalem, and the clear legal position that unilateral decisions on Jerusalem are null and void. France asks no further changes and calls on the Council to act unitedly and promptly.
messages.Italy: Italy supports the revised draft, which reflects the necessary concern at recent decisions on Jerusalem, reaffirms that Jerusalem is a final-status issue, and rejects unilateral changes while preserving the two-State solution. We welcome the balanced language condemning violence and terrorism while calling for de-escalation and renewed negotiations. Italy will vote in favour if the text is put to the vote.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the current text and welcomes that our key concerns on Jerusalem have been incorporated, including the expression of deep regret at recent decisions, the reaffirmation that actions altering Jerusalem’s character or status have no legal effect, and the call on all States to refrain from establishing diplomatic missions in Jerusalem. We believe the Council should speak with one voice and make clear that unilateral actions cannot prejudge final status negotiations. Japan will support the draft as it stands and urges all members to do likewise.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports the current text, which reflects our key concerns on Jerusalem, including deep regret at recent decisions, the nullity of actions altering the Holy City’s character or status, and compliance with resolutions 2334 (2016) and 478 (1980). We welcome the balanced call for de-escalation, respect for the historic status quo, and resumed direct negotiations without preconditions. Kazakhstan encourages all Council members to unite behind this draft.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the current draft as it stands. It reflects our core position: Jerusalem is a final status issue, unilateral decisions cannot prejudge negotiations, settlement activity must cease, and the parties must resume direct talks on the basis of the Madrid principles, the Arab Peace Initiative and the Quartet Roadmap. We welcome the references to Quartet and Egyptian-Russian efforts and see no need for further changes at this stage; we call on all members to support the text.
messages.Senegal: Senegal supports the revised draft as it now clearly reaffirms the illegality of settlements, the 1967 lines, and the nullity of unilateral changes to Jerusalem. These elements reflect our principled position and resolution 2334 (2016). We urge the Council to preserve this balanced text and proceed to a vote without further weakening.
messages.Sweden: Sweden supports the current text as revised. We welcome that our key concerns have been incorporated: Jerusalem-related decisions have no legal effect, all States should refrain from diplomatic missions in Jerusalem under resolution 478, settlement activity must cease, and Israel's obligations as the occupying Power are clear. This is a lawful and balanced basis for Council action, and we encourage all members to support it.
messages.Ukraine: Ukraine thanks the penholder for incorporating our proposals on resolution 478 and on the null and void character of unilateral decisions concerning Jerusalem. The current text is balanced: it reaffirms the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines, condemns violence and terrorism, and takes account of Israel's legitimate security concerns and the Palestinian right to statehood. Ukraine will vote in favour and urges all Council members to support the draft.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the current text and welcomes the incorporation of our proposals on Jerusalem’s status and on diplomatic missions. We believe the draft appropriately reaffirms that Jerusalem is a final status issue while calling for de-escalation, accountability and a resumption of negotiations that take account of Israel’s legitimate security concerns and the Palestinian right to statehood. The United Kingdom has no further changes to request and would vote in favour if the text is put to the Council.
messages.United States of America: The current text remains unacceptable. The United States cannot support a resolution that condemns a sovereign decision and purports to nullify it, or that calls on states not to establish diplomatic missions in Jerusalem. If PP9, OP5, and OP6 are retained, we will veto. We are prepared to work on a balanced text that reaffirms Jerusalem as a final-status issue, calls on all parties to avoid unilateral steps, and condemns violence and incitement by all sides.
messages.Uruguay: Uruguay supports the current text as revised. It incorporates our red lines on Jerusalem and the 1967 lines while maintaining a balanced call for de-escalation, accountability and resumed negotiations. We urge the Council to speak with one voice and all parties to comply with resolution 2334 (2016).

reasons.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia’s established foreign policy is strongly pro-Palestinian and supportive of international law, UN resolutions, and the two-State solution; the draft aligns with those priorities despite balanced language on violence and security.
reasons.China: China supported the Egyptian draft and would vote in favour, consistent with its long-standing position on the two-State solution, settlements and Jerusalem’s final status. It would likely reserve its explanation for after the vote, particularly given the expected U.S. veto.
reasons.Egypt: Egypt sponsored the draft and would vote in favour to reaffirm international law, Jerusalem’s final-status character, the illegality of settlements, and the two-State solution while also condemning violence and terrorism. A pre-vote statement reinforces its role as sponsor and regional mediator.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the two-State solution, international law and relevant Security Council resolutions, and it had already supported the draft in negotiations. The draft is balanced enough to back, as it also condemns violence and calls for negotiations without directly targeting the United States.
reasons.France: France supports the Egyptian draft because it reaffirms resolution 2334, the two-State parameters, Jerusalem’s final status, and calls for de-escalation while condemning violence. A yes vote is consistent with France’s established position on this agenda item.
reasons.Italy: Italy’s established position supports the two-State solution and the EU line that Jerusalem is final status and the status quo must be preserved; the Egyptian draft is balanced by condemning violence and rocket attacks and calling for negotiations, so Italy would vote in favour.
reasons.Japan: Japan consistently supports a two-State solution and voted for resolution 2334; the draft reaffirms that framework while also condemning violence and recognizing Israel’s security concerns, so it aligns with Japan’s position and last-round support.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supported the Egyptian draft and, consistent with its established position and the actual Council vote, would vote in favour. It would not take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia supports the Egyptian draft, which is consistent with resolution 2334 (2016) and its opposition to unilateral changes to Jerusalem’s status. It would likely reserve its explanation for after the expected U.S. veto rather than speak before the vote.
reasons.Senegal: Senegal has consistently supported resolution 2334, Palestinian statehood, and a two-State solution; this draft reaffirms those principles while also calling for de-escalation and condemning violence and terrorism. Senegal therefore votes in favour.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden consistently supports a rules-based international order, the two-State solution, and the Council’s position that Jerusalem is a final-status issue; the draft reaffirms resolution 2334 and condemns violence on both sides. Sweden therefore would vote yes.
reasons.Ukraine: Ukraine consistently supports UN resolutions on the Middle East and voted for resolution 2334; this balanced draft affirms international law and the two-State solution while condemning violence. A yes vote with an explanation matches Ukraine’s established diplomatic practice.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: UK supported the draft in negotiations because it aligns with its long-standing policy on the two-State solution, Jerusalem, settlements, and condemnation of violence. As a P5 member, it would vote in favour rather than veto or abstain.
reasons.United States of America: The United States would veto this draft on 18 December 2017, consistent with its opposition to Council action on Jerusalem/final status after the U.S. recognition decision and its broader policy of shielding Israel from one-sided UN measures. The remaining settlement language and final-status parameters also make a U.S. affirmative vote implausible.
reasons.Uruguay: Uruguay consistently supports international law, resolution 2334 (2016), and the two-State solution; the draft aligns with those positions and its last-round support. Historically, Uruguay voted in favour of the December 2017 Jerusalem draft that the United States vetoed.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia (Plurinational State of) will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because it reaffirms the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force, the illegality of Israeli settlement activities, and the principle that Jerusalem remains a final status issue to be resolved through negotiations consistent with international law and the relevant United Nations resolutions. My delegation condemns all violence against civilians, including rocket attacks, and calls for restraint and de-escalation. At the same time, the Council cannot remain silent before unilateral actions that alter the character and status of Jerusalem or before the continuing occupation and settlement of Palestinian territory, which imperil the two-State solution and peace itself. Bolivia will continue to defend the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people and a just, lasting and comprehensive peace based on the 1967 lines.
before.Egypt: Egypt votes in favour of this draft resolution, which we have submitted in response to the dangerous escalation in the region and the urgent need for the Council to speak clearly and responsibly. The text before the Council is balanced and grounded in international law and existing resolutions, including resolution 2334 (2016). It reaffirms the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force, the illegality of settlements, and the principle that Jerusalem is a final status issue whose status and historic character must be respected and preserved. It also condemns all violence against civilians, including acts of terror and rocket attacks, and calls for calm, restraint and accountability. Egypt has consistently shouldered its responsibilities for peace and stability in the Middle East, and we believe this resolution can help de-escalate tensions and create conditions for the resumption of credible negotiations on the basis of the two-State solution, the Arab Peace Initiative, the Madrid principles and the Quartet Roadmap. We call upon all members of the Council to support this balanced text and to uphold the Council’s responsibilities.
before.Ethiopia: Ethiopia votes in favour of this draft. We support the call for immediate de-escalation and for all parties to refrain from violence, incitement and provocative actions. The draft reaffirms the two-State solution based on the 4 June 1967 lines, the final status character of Jerusalem, and the need to preserve the historic status quo of the Holy Sites. We urge the parties to resume credible direct negotiations without delay, and we support the constructive role of Egypt, the Quartet and other regional and international partners.
before.France: France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The text is balanced and necessary: it reaffirms the parameters of international law and of this Council, including that Jerusalem is a final status issue, that the historic status quo at the Holy Sites must be respected, that settlement activity is illegal, and that all violence and incitement must cease. At this grave moment, France calls on all parties to exercise restraint and to avoid any unilateral action that could prejudge final status negotiations. The Council must speak clearly in support of the two-State solution.
before.Italy: Mr. President, Italy will vote in favour of this draft resolution. Italy has consistently supported a just, lasting and comprehensive peace in the Middle East based on the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within secure and recognized borders based on the 4 June 1967 lines, with agreed swaps. Jerusalem is a final status issue, and the historic status quo at the Holy Sites must be respected. Italy remains concerned by any unilateral action that could prejudge the outcome of final status negotiations or further inflame tensions. At the same time, we condemn all acts of violence against civilians, including terrorism and rocket attacks, and we call on all parties to exercise restraint, avoid incitement and return to credible direct negotiations. This draft resolution is balanced: it recalls resolution 2334 (2016), addresses the situation on the ground, and calls for de-escalation and the resumption of negotiations. For these reasons, Italy supports it.
before.Japan: Japan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because the text is balanced, reaffirms resolution 2334 (2016), and clearly states that Jerusalem is a final status issue to be resolved through negotiations and that no unilateral changes should prejudge the outcome. It also rightly condemns all violence against civilians, including rocket attacks against Israel, and recognizes Israel’s legitimate security concerns, while calling for de-escalation, respect for the historic status quo at the Holy Sites, and the resumption of credible direct negotiations without delay or preconditions. Japan urges all parties to exercise restraint, refrain from inflammatory rhetoric and provocative actions, and work toward a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines with agreed swaps, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security.
before.Senegal: Senegal will vote in favour of this draft resolution. It is consistent with our principled position and with resolution 2334 (2016): Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem, are illegal under international law and must cease. We reaffirm that Jerusalem is a final-status issue and that the historic status quo of the Holy Sites must be respected. We call for immediate de-escalation and condemn all acts of violence and terrorism against civilians. Only credible negotiations leading to two States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security within secure and recognized borders on the basis of the 1967 lines can bring a just and lasting peace.
before.Sweden: Mr. President, Sweden will vote in favour of the draft resolution. The status of Jerusalem is a final status issue that must be resolved through negotiations between the parties, consistent with international law and the relevant Security Council resolutions, including resolution 2334. Unilateral steps that prejudge the outcome of final status negotiations undermine the prospects for peace. Sweden remains firmly committed to the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines, with Jerusalem as the capital of both States through agreement, and we condemn all acts of violence and incitement, including rocket attacks against Israel. We call on all parties to exercise restraint and to return to credible negotiations. The Council must uphold its resolutions and the international consensus, and Egypt’s draft does so. Sweden therefore votes in favour.
before.Ukraine: Mr. President, Ukraine will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We do so because we consistently uphold the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force, respect for international humanitarian law and relevant Security Council resolutions, including resolution 2334 (2016). We are gravely concerned by the recent escalation and loss of civilian life in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza. We condemn all violence and terrorism, including rocket attacks against Israel, and call on all parties to exercise restraint and refrain from provocative actions and inflammatory rhetoric. Ukraine remains committed to the two-State solution based on the 4 June 1967 lines with agreed swaps, with Jerusalem as a final status issue to be resolved through negotiations and with respect for the historic status quo at the Holy Sites. We call on the parties to resume credible direct negotiations and urge all members of the Council to act in a manner that does not prejudge final status issues or undermine trust.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. Our position is clear: Jerusalem is a final status issue that must be resolved through negotiations between the parties, and we respect the historic status quo at the Holy Sites. We remain committed to the two-State solution based on the 4 June 1967 lines, with agreed swaps, and to Israel’s security and the Palestinian right to statehood. Settlement activity is illegal under international law and corrodes the prospects for peace. We condemn all acts of violence and terrorism, including rocket attacks against Israel, and call on all parties to de-escalate and return to credible direct negotiations. This draft is balanced and consistent with resolution 2334 (2016), and the United Kingdom supports it.
before.United States of America: The United States has engaged in good faith and appreciates the efforts to adjust this text. But we cannot support a resolution that remains unbalanced, that seeks through the Security Council to prejudge or impose parameters on final status issues, and that would not advance the direct negotiations the parties need. The United States will vote against this draft.
before.Uruguay: Uruguay will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so in consistency with our vote on resolution 2334 (2016) and with our unwavering commitment to international law, the Charter of the United Nations and the two-State solution. The text before us rightly calls for immediate de-escalation and calm, condemns all violence against civilians, including acts of terror and rocket attacks, and reaffirms that Israeli settlements in occupied Palestinian territory have no legal validity. It also reaffirms that Jerusalem is a final status issue to be resolved through negotiations and that the historic status quo and multi-religious character of the Holy Sites must be preserved. Uruguay emphasizes that unilateral actions cannot prejudge the outcome of final status negotiations. We urge the parties to resume credible direct negotiations without delay and without preconditions, with the support of the Quartet and regional partners, including Egypt and the Russian Federation. The Security Council must uphold its responsibilities and act to preserve the prospects for peace.

after.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Mr. President, Bolivia regrets that this Council has again been prevented from discharging its responsibilities by the negative vote of a permanent member. Fourteen members voted in favour of a balanced text rooted in international law and in resolution 2334 (2016). That isolated veto cannot erase Israel’s obligations as the occupying Power, nor the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force, nor the illegality of settlements and unilateral changes to Jerusalem that prejudge final status. Bolivia rejects the United States decision on Jerusalem as a unilateral act that inflames tensions and undermines peace. We reaffirm that Jerusalem is a final status issue, that the historic status quo at the Holy Sites must be preserved, and that there can be no recognition of changes to the 4 June 1967 lines. My delegation condemns all violence against civilians, including rocket attacks, while recalling that occupation and impunity are root causes. We call for de-escalation, accountability and credible negotiations leading to two States, Israel and Palestine, with East Jerusalem as the capital of Palestine. Bolivia will continue to stand with the Palestinian people and with international law. This Council must not accept a veto that obstructs peace and justice.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution. We regret that the draft resolution was not adopted.

The question of Palestine is at the core of the Middle East issue. The recent tensions, including those relating to Jerusalem, have once again shown that unilateral actions cannot bring peace and will only aggravate confrontation. China firmly supports the just cause of the Palestinian people and their legitimate national rights. We oppose all settlement activities in the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem, which are illegal under international law and inconsistent with resolution 2334 (2016). Jerusalem is a final status issue to be resolved through negotiations between the parties, and the historic status quo of the Holy Sites should be respected.

China condemns all acts of violence against civilians, including acts of terror and rocket attacks. We call on all parties to exercise restraint, refrain from provocative actions and inflammatory rhetoric, de-escalate the situation and return to credible negotiations on the basis of the relevant United Nations resolutions, the principle of land for peace, the Arab Peace Initiative and the Quartet Roadmap, with a view to achieving two States, Palestine and Israel, living side by side in peace within secure and recognized borders.

The Security Council should play its due role in the Middle East peace process. China will continue to work with the international community to promote a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in the Middle East.
after.Egypt:
Mr. President,

Egypt thanks the members of the Council who supported the draft resolution we submitted. We deeply regret that the Security Council was unable to adopt it owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. The result — 14 votes in favour and one against — is clear and speaks for itself. It reflects the broad international consensus in support of international law, the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force, the illegality of settlements, and the principle that Jerusalem is a final status issue to be resolved through negotiations.

The draft was balanced and responsible. It condemned all violence against civilians, including acts of terror and rocket attacks. It recognized Israel’s legitimate security concerns. It called for de-escalation, restraint, and the resumption of credible direct negotiations without preconditions. It also reaffirmed the historic status quo at the Holy Sites in Jerusalem and rejected unilateral actions that prejudge final status negotiations. None of these principles should have been controversial.

The use of the veto does not diminish the validity of international law, nor does it alter the legal status of East Jerusalem or the fact that settlements are illegal. It does not erase the international consensus or the rights of the Palestinian people. The Security Council has missed an opportunity to shoulder its responsibilities at a dangerous moment. Egypt will not abandon its historical responsibilities. We will continue to defend the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including their right to an independent, sovereign State with East Jerusalem as its capital, and to work with all partners to revive a credible peace process. We call upon all parties to exercise restraint and upon the international community to uphold its obligations.

Thank you.
after.France:
Mr. President, France voted in favour of this draft resolution and regrets that it could not be adopted because of the negative vote of a permanent member, despite the support of 14 members of this Council.

The text before us was balanced and responsible. It called for immediate de-escalation and restraint. It condemned all violence against civilians, including rocket attacks against Israel, and it took account of Israel’s legitimate security concerns. At the same time, it reaffirmed the foundations of a just peace: the illegality of settlements under international law, respect for resolution 2334 (2016), the final status character of Jerusalem, the need to preserve the historic status quo at the Holy Sites, and the imperative of direct negotiations without preconditions.

This veto does not diminish the obligations of the parties under international law and under the resolutions of this Council. Nor does it weaken the international consensus in support of the two-State solution based on the 4 June 1967 lines, with agreed swaps, with two States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security. France calls on all parties to refrain from unilateral actions and inflammatory rhetoric, to restore calm, and to resume credible negotiations on all final status issues. France will continue to work with its partners, including in the European Union, the Quartet and the region, to preserve the prospect of peace.
after.Kazakhstan:
Mr. President,

Kazakhstan voted in favour of the draft resolution. We did so because the text was balanced and grounded in international law and in Security Council resolution 2334 (2016). It called for immediate de-escalation, condemned all violence against civilians, reaffirmed the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines, and upheld the principle that Jerusalem is a final status issue to be resolved through negotiations.

Kazakhstan regrets that the Council was unable to adopt this resolution. We believe the Security Council should be able to speak with one voice in support of international law, restraint and the resumption of a credible peace process. We call on all parties to refrain from unilateral actions, incitement and inflammatory rhetoric, and to return to direct negotiations on all final status issues. Kazakhstan will continue to support the efforts of the Quartet, Egypt, the Russian Federation and other partners aimed at achieving a just, lasting and comprehensive peace in the Middle East.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President, the Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Egypt. We did so because the text was balanced and firmly grounded in international law and in the existing decisions of the Security Council, including resolution 2334 (2016). It reaffirmed the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force, the illegality of Israeli settlement activity, the need to preserve the historic status quo at the Holy Sites, and the principle that Jerusalem is a final status issue to be settled through negotiations. It also condemned violence against civilians, including acts of terror and rocket attacks against Israel, and called for de-escalation and the resumption of direct Israeli-Palestinian negotiations. That is why an overwhelming majority of Council members supported it.

We regret that the Security Council has once again been unable to speak with a single voice on one of the most sensitive issues of the Middle East. The use of the veto does not alter the legal and political realities we face. The status of Jerusalem cannot be decided unilaterally, and attempts to prejudge final status issues through unilateral actions are unacceptable. The veto also does not relieve the parties or the Council of the obligation to work for a just, lasting and comprehensive settlement on the basis of the two-State solution, the Madrid principles, the Arab Peace Initiative and the relevant United Nations resolutions.

The Russian Federation, as a member of the Quartet and a permanent member of the Security Council, will continue to work with all parties and regional and international partners, including Egypt, to de-escalate tensions and to bring the Palestinians and Israelis back to credible direct negotiations. We have consistently supported such negotiations, including through our proposal to hold a meeting between the leaders of Palestine and Israel in Moscow. We call on the parties to exercise restraint, avoid provocative actions and inflammatory rhetoric, and to demonstrate by their conduct that they remain committed to peace. The Council must not remain passive. We will continue to advocate the earliest resumption of a meaningful negotiating process and a unified international position in support of peace.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr. President,

The United Kingdom regrets that the Security Council has not been able to adopt this resolution, despite the clear support of fourteen members. We voted in favour because the text was balanced, consistent with resolution 2334 (2016), and reflected the international consensus on the need for de-escalation and a return to credible negotiations.

The United Kingdom’s position remains clear: Jerusalem is a final status issue that must be resolved through negotiations between the parties, and the historic status quo at the Holy Sites must be respected. Settlement activity is illegal under international law and corrodes the prospects for a two-State solution. We condemn all acts of violence and terrorism, including rocket attacks against Israel, and call on all parties to exercise restraint, avoid incitement and provocative actions, and work in good faith towards direct negotiations.

The Council’s inability to act today should not be an excuse for unilateral steps by any party. The United Kingdom will continue to work with all partners, including the United States, to support a just and lasting peace based on two States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security within secure and recognised borders, based on the 4 June 1967 lines with agreed swaps.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States has exercised its veto because this Council should not be used to impose parameters on final status issues or to prejudge the outcome of negotiations that only the parties can conclude. The text before us was unbalanced. It sought to use the Security Council to dictate the terms of a settlement and to pass judgment on Jerusalem, even as the United States has simply recognized the reality that Jerusalem is Israel’s capital. That recognition does not prejudge final status talks; it does not, in itself, determine final borders; and it is fully consistent with the United States’ longstanding commitment to a comprehensive peace and a two-State solution, if the parties agree.

We remain committed to direct negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians, without preconditions, on all final status issues. But the United States will not support a resolution that is more about attacking Israel than advancing peace. This vote will not be forgotten. The United States will continue to stand with Israel and will not be told by any country where we place our embassy or how we exercise our sovereign rights.

Thank you.
